title: Connect an AI agent
subtitle: A connected agent draws and tends this map for you.

manualPathHint: This is a browser session, so fill in the absolute folder path yourself: replace the [absolute path to your my-folder] slot in the snippet with your real path.
genericHint: Any other MCP client registers with the same launch command and arguments. Use “Verify connection” above rather than running a check by hand.

otherToolsClaudeDesktopNote: Register manually in Settings → Developer (dedicated extension later)
step1Desc: Press the button for your tool and it's ready to read and write this folder with you.
step2Desc: Quit and reopen the tool you just connected. The others can stay as they are.
step3Desc: Once the agent starts reading this map, it shows up here.
actionFailed: That did not work. Press it again.
replaceCodexConfigDone: Copied · review and replace existing config.toml
deeplinkWebNote: One-click for Cursor needs the folder path.
serverLine: Atlas's agent-connection (MCP) server is not a program that stays running. Your agent starts it on this computer only when it is needed and shuts it down with the conversation. It opens no port and makes no network request. The agent itself may talk to its own provider when you ask it to.
copiedToast: Config copied: paste it into your tool to connect.
serverUnavailableTitle: Only saving the config for you is out of reach here
serverUnavailableDesc: Your agent connects to the folder, not to Atlas: it starts the MCP server in its own session and reads and writes that folder. A browser just cannot know where the folder you opened actually lives, so it cannot save the config file for you. Tell it the path and the working config is built right here. Open the same folder in the desktop app and it is one button instead.
manualVaultLabel: ① Absolute path to your folder
manualCheckoutLabel: ② Path to your ontology-atlas source checkout
manualCheckoutHint: That is where the MCP server your agent starts lives. The desktop app carries it for you instead.
manualCloneCta: No checkout yet: copy the git clone command
manualCloneCopied: Copied · put the resulting folder path in ②
manualShapeOnlyNote: This only checks the shape of the path: whether it is absolute, and free of a tilde (~) or stray quotes. The folder your browser opened and the path you typed here cannot be compared, so the browser cannot prove they are the same folder. Whether it actually connects is what the verify command below tells you.
manualPathConfirmation: I confirm that the absolute folder path above is the same vault folder I opened in this browser.
manualIssueTilde: A tilde (~) is not expanded inside a config file, so it would silently fail. Use the real path (starting with /Users/…) that pwd prints in your terminal.
manualIssueRelative: An absolute path is required: start with a slash, like /Users/… (or C:\… on Windows).
manualIssueMultiline: One path only: this contains a line break.
manualFileHint: Save this as {file} in the folder you open your agent from. The path inside is absolute, so it reaches the same folder from anywhere.
manualNotReadyNote: Copying unlocks once both paths are filled in and you confirm the vault path. A config with placeholders or an unconfirmed folder does not connect, so it is not handed over.
manualCliLabel: Prefer not to create files by hand: this one line writes the Claude Code (.mcp.json) and Codex (.codex/config.toml) configs. Missing files only; existing ones are left alone. Cursor and Antigravity read different files, so use the copy above for those.
manualRestartNote: Once saved, quit and reopen your agent: that is when it reads the new config. The verify command below tells you whether it connected.
copyFailed: Copy failed: the clipboard was blocked
